── NESSA'S WEEK ──
Nessa is 41 and new to running, aiming to run the whole Corrowmore Harvest 5K on 15 November without walking. Nessa walk-runs three mornings a week (Monday, Wednesday and Saturday) and walks the dog most days.
Recent weeks: 6.8, 7.3 km
This week: 2.8 km over 1 run. Missed 2 of 3 planned runs.
Body: "Came down with a cold on Tuesday that turned into a fever, 38.4 on Wednesday night. No fever since Friday but still coughing and blocked up."
Feeling: "Wiped out."
Asks: "Can I do all three runs next week and add the two I missed?"

── THE DRAFT ──
Tells Nessa: Do not make up the missed runs. …
Answers: (1) No to both. Runs you miss are not owed back. (2) Keep to your usual three days, and only run if you have no fever and the cough is easing. Monday is a walk and Wednesday is a lighter walk-run with one-minute runs.
Safety flag: See your GP if the fever or cough gets worse
Safety flag: Stop straight away if you have chest pain or feel dizzy
Next week:
Mon: other, 20 min, easy walk with the dog, no running. Gives your body two more days to…
Tue: rest. An easy dog walk is fine. Getting over the cold comes first.
Wed: easy, 21 min, walk-run: 5 min brisk walk, then 8 x 1 min easy run with 1 min walk…
Thu: rest. An easy dog walk is fine. Gives you a day to check how Wednesday's run sat.
Fri: rest. An easy dog walk is fine. Two clear days before Saturday help while you are…
Sat: easy, 23 min, walk-run: 5 min brisk walk, then 6 x 2 min easy run with 1 min walk…
Sun: rest. An easy dog walk is fine. A full rest day to round off your first week back.
